entities.summary: Diogenes of Smyrna was a Cynic philosopher and ascetic of the Classical era, active in the Hellenistic world of the 3rd century BCE. Born in Smyrna, Asia Minor, and educated in Athens, he became a prominent figure in the intellectual and cultural landscape of the Mediterranean, known for his uncompromising adherence to the principles of Cynicism. His teachings and lifestyle, which emphasized self-sufficiency and the rejection of luxury and social convention, influenced a wide range of thinkers and philosophers, including the Stoics and the Epicureans. Through his writings and public debates, Diogenes of Smyrna contributed to the development of Western philosophy, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continues to inspire and provoke to this day. As a testament to his enduring influence, Diogenes' philosophy remains a subject of study and debate among scholars and students of classical thought, offering insights into the human condition and the search for meaning and purpose in a complex and often uncertain world.
